threads.body: [General] Keep this stable configuration path exact-only. `CommonConfig` supplies the existing `general.http.client.*_captured_headers` lists, and the flat `otel.instrumentation.http.client.capture-*-headers` properties map to them; wrapping those lists in `IncludeExclude` reinterprets existing `*`/`?` values as globs. A previously inert `*` can therefore capture every request or response header, including credentials, although migration of these configuration surfaces is explicitly deferred. Preserve an exact-name path for `configure(...)` until the upstream schema is migrated.

replies.body:
Good catch, and it was worse than "reinterprets": these settings never documented `*` as capturing everything, so a previously inert value became capture-everything on a stable surface.

Fixed in 1572a0077b. `CapturedHttpHeaders` now has a `createExact` factory that stores the configured names as a literal set and never builds a selector, and both deprecated setters plus `configure(CommonConfig)` route through it. So the flat properties and the `general.http.client.*_captured_headers` lists keep matching literally, with no wildcard carve-out at all.

Worth noting why there is no lone-`*` special case here, since `SelectorConfig.resolveLegacyLiteral` does have one. That carve-out exists only because the phase 1 settings documented `*` as capture-all, so preserving it was bug-for-bug compatibility. The HTTP docs only ever said "List of HTTP request headers to capture", so the same carve-out would have been a widening rather than a preservation.

The regression test I had added asserted the old behavior (it literally asserted that `*` captured `authorization: secret`); it now asserts the opposite.

threads.body: [General] Restore a literal-name representation for legacy callers. This helper currently only represents `IncludeExclude` selectors, so the deprecated setters and stable `configure(CommonConfig)` paths must pass through `DeprecatedCaptureNames`, which drops names containing `*`/`?`. That changes their previous exact-name behavior (for example, a literal `*` header can no longer be captured) and reintroduces the regression that commit `1572a0077b` fixed. Add the `createExact(...)` path from that fix, route both deprecated setters and `CommonConfig` through it, and update the corresponding docs/tests to assert literal matching.

replies.body:
Addressed in 4e5a616b33aefcf7606e0f0cdb8c6dfcadac634e.

Analysis: The selector-only representation cannot preserve legacy exact-name semantics because DeprecatedCaptureNames removes glob metacharacters. Restoring a dedicated exact-name representation lets deprecated setters and CommonConfig retain their previous literal behavior while the new IncludeExclude APIs continue to support patterns.

Upsides: Preserves backward compatibility, prevents accidental wildcard expansion, supports literal metacharacter header names, and documents and tests both API behaviors.

Downsides: CapturedHttpHeaders must maintain separate exact-name and selector representations.
